investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Available Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the agent pod because 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the eval runner never received a VM ID or a ready state, so all required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) is absent and the expected-output contract is entirely unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the two nodes that match the pod's affinity/selector. With 0 of 6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote-agent pod creation attempt times out unscheduled. This is an infrastructure-layer resource exhaustion on the production Kubernetes cluster, not a code defect in the eval runner or a regression in the eval configuration files. The eval failure is a direct consequence of the scheduling failure; no evidence of a user-traffic or production incident signal is present in the packet, so impact is scoped to the observability eval at this time.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots are fully consumed on the two affinity-eligible nodes: the scheduler message 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' on both eligible nodes is unambiguous. No preemption victims were found, meaning all existing VM pods are non-preemptible or at equal/higher priority.

Secondary — the node affinity or node selector on the remote-agent pod restricts scheduling to only 2 of 6 nodes, leaving no fallback capacity even if other nodes have free resources. The 4 non-matching nodes cannot be used regardless of their available capacity.

Tertiary — a prior remote-agent pod (or multiple pods) may have been created and not cleaned up, holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and preventing new allocations. The eval runner uses withCleanup, but a previous failed or leaked run could have left pods running.
Lower confidence — the cluster may have scaled down or lost one of the affinity-eligible nodes between runs, reducing total kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity below the minimum needed for a new probe pod.

investigation.summary: The model-matrix eval check failed because exactly one of two configured models, aura-gpt-5-5, received a 502 Bad Gateway from the AURA runtime harness wrapping an Anthropic 429 Too Many Requests error. investigation.rootCause: The AURA runtime harness returned HTTP 502 for the POST /api/agents/[REDACTED]/runtime/test request targeting model aura-gpt-5-5. The 502 body explicitly identifies the internal cause as a rate_limit error: the upstream Anthropic API responded with 429 Too Many Requests and the message "AURA is temporarily unable to reach the model provider. This is an issue on our side, not with your account or credits. Please try again shortly." This caused the eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1936 model loop) to record ok=false for aura-gpt-5-5, setting allPassed=false and failedModelCount=1, which violated the expected-output contract assertions at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json lines 333–334. investigation.title: image-generation-stream Eval Failure: OpenAI Billing Hard Limit Reached on /api/generate/image/stream
investigation.summary: The image-generation-stream eval failed because the OpenAI API returned a hard billing limit error (billing_hard_limit_reached) when the eval runner called /api/generate/image/stream, causing the stream to terminate with a generation_error frame instead of a generation_completed frame and no image URL artifact. Both required contract assertions — frameTypes containing "generation_completed" and imageUrlPresent equaling true — were violated as a direct consequence of this upstream billing rejection.
investigation.rootCause: The OpenAI account or API key used by the eval runner has hit its configured billing hard limit. When the runner called /api/generate/image/stream (evidence: source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1977-1985, line 1984), OpenAI rejected the image generation request with error code "billing_hard_limit_reached" and type "billing_limit_user_error". The stream emitted generation_start and generation_progress frames before receiving the error, then emitted a generation_error frame with GENERATION_FAILED and terminated without ever emitting generation_completed or an image URL. This is an eval infrastructure failure caused by an external billing constraint on the OpenAI account; no evidence of a user-traffic or production incident is present in the supplied packet.
proof: failed-check.message: OpenAI error body contains code=billing_hard_limit_reached and type=billing_limit_user_error, directly explaining why generation did not complete.

failed-check.evidence: frameTypes observed = [generation_start, generation_start, generation_progress, generation_error, message]; generation_completed is absent; imageUrlPresent=false. Both contract assertions fail as a downstream consequence of the billing rejection.

failed-check.evidence: The generation_error frame carries data.code=GENERATION_FAILED and data.message containing the full OpenAI billing error JSON, confirming the error originated at the OpenAI API boundary.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=1590 — the call returned in under 2 seconds, consistent with an immediate API-level rejection rather than a timeout or network failure.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1977-1985 (line 1984): The runner calls apiSse(args, "/api/generate/image/stream", ...) with model defaulting to gpt-image-2 (line 1986), confirming the exact endpoint and model that received the billing rejection.
expected-output.contract: Contract requires frameTypes to contain generation_completed and imageUrlPresent=true; neither was satisfied because the stream terminated at generation_error.
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — OpenAI billing hard limit exhausted on the account or API key used by the eval runner. The error code billing_hard_limit_reached is an explicit, structured OpenAI API response indicating the account's spending cap has been reached. No image generation requests will succeed until the limit is raised or the billing period resets.

SECONDARY — The eval runner is using a dedicated eval/CI OpenAI API key whose billing limit is set lower than the cost of sustained eval runs, and that key's limit was reached before this run. This would explain why the failure is isolated to this check and no sibling checks share the same message.

TERTIARY — A misconfigured or rotated AURA_STATUS_IMAGE_MODEL environment variable caused the runner to use a model (gpt-image-2 by default per line 1986) that is billed at a higher rate, accelerating limit exhaustion. This is speculative; the error message does not reference the model.

investigation.title: published-observability-snapshot Eval Failure: Stale GitHub Actions Snapshot (snapshotAgeMinutes 378 > max 300)
investigation.summary: The AURA observability eval for published-observability-snapshot failed because the snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json was 378 minutes old at eval time, exceeding the contract's maximum allowed age of 300 minutes. This is a localized eval failure against the published snapshot JSON endpoint; all three sibling public-website checks (public-observability-page, public-models-page, public-marketing-pages) passed, confirming the public website itself is reachable and this failure is isolated to snapshot freshness.
investigation.rootCause: The GitHub Actions workflow responsible for regenerating and publishing the observability snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json did not run within the 300-minute window required by the expected-output contract (infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 482: snapshotAgeMinutes max 300). The snapshot was 378 minutes old when the eval ran at 2026-07-23T07:25:40Z, meaning the last successful publish occurred approximately 6 hours and 18 minutes prior. The workflow schedule, a transient runner failure, a skipped or cancelled run, or a publishing step failure are the most likely upstream causes, but the exact trigger cannot be determined from the supplied evidence alone.

failed-check.evidence: snapshotAgeMinutes=378, maxAgeMinutes=300, source='github-actions', hasLiveSource=true, generatedAtPresent=true — the snapshot exists and was produced by github-actions but is stale.

sibling.public-observability-page, sibling.public-models-page, sibling.public-marketing-pages: all three sibling checks passed, ruling out a broad public-website infrastructure failure and localizing the issue to the snapshot publishing pipeline.

possibleCauses: The GitHub Actions workflow that publishes the observability snapshot was not triggered or did not complete successfully within the last 300 minutes, leaving the previously published snapshot in place (supported by source='github-actions' and snapshotAgeMinutes=378 in failed-check.evidence).

The GitHub Actions workflow ran but the publish step (e.g., the GitHub Pages deploy step) failed silently, so the snapshot file at the snapshotUrl was not updated even though a workflow run may appear in the Actions UI.

The workflow schedule was skipped, delayed, or cancelled — for example due to a GitHub Actions queue backlog, a branch protection event, or a manual cancellation — causing the snapshot to age past the 300-minute threshold.

A configuration mismatch exists between the registry's staleAfterMinutes=360 (infra/evals/status/features.json line 383) and the contract's snapshotAgeMinutes max=300 (infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 482): the registry considers the check stale after 360 minutes but the eval contract fails it at 300 minutes, meaning a snapshot between 300 and 360 minutes old will fail the eval but not be considered stale by the registry. This discrepancy may cause confusion about the expected refresh cadence but does not by itself explain the 378-minute age.

investigations.title: image-generation-stream Eval Failure: OpenAI Billing Hard Limit Reached on /api/generate/image/stream
investigations.summary: The image-generation-stream eval failed because the OpenAI API returned a hard billing limit error (billing_hard_limit_reached) when the eval runner called /api/generate/image/stream, causing the stream to terminate with a generation_error frame instead of a generation_completed frame and no image URL artifact. Both required contract assertions — frameTypes containing "generation_completed" and imageUrlPresent equaling true — were violated as a direct consequence of this upstream billing rejection.
investigations.rootCause: The OpenAI account or API key used by the eval runner has hit its configured billing hard limit. When the runner called /api/generate/image/stream (evidence: source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1977-1985, line 1984), OpenAI rejected the image generation request with error code "billing_hard_limit_reached" and type "billing_limit_user_error". The stream emitted generation_start and generation_progress frames before receiving the error, then emitted a generation_error frame with GENERATION_FAILED and terminated without ever emitting generation_completed or an image URL. This is an eval infrastructure failure caused by an external billing constraint on the OpenAI account; no evidence of a user-traffic or production incident is present in the supplied packet.
proof: failed-check.message: OpenAI error body contains code=billing_hard_limit_reached and type=billing_limit_user_error, directly explaining why generation did not complete.

failed-check.evidence: frameTypes observed = [generation_start, generation_start, generation_progress, generation_error, message]; generation_completed is absent; imageUrlPresent=false. Both contract assertions fail as a downstream consequence of the billing rejection.

failed-check.evidence: The generation_error frame carries data.code=GENERATION_FAILED and data.message containing the full OpenAI billing error JSON, confirming the error originated at the OpenAI API boundary.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=1590 — the call returned in under 2 seconds, consistent with an immediate API-level rejection rather than a timeout or network failure.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1977-1985 (line 1984): The runner calls apiSse(args, "/api/generate/image/stream", ...) with model defaulting to gpt-image-2 (line 1986), confirming the exact endpoint and model that received the billing rejection.
expected-output.contract: Contract requires frameTypes to contain generation_completed and imageUrlPresent=true; neither was satisfied because the stream terminated at generation_error.
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — OpenAI billing hard limit exhausted on the account or API key used by the eval runner. The error code billing_hard_limit_reached is an explicit, structured OpenAI API response indicating the account's spending cap has been reached. No image generation requests will succeed until the limit is raised or the billing period resets.

SECONDARY — The eval runner is using a dedicated eval/CI OpenAI API key whose billing limit is set lower than the cost of sustained eval runs, and that key's limit was reached before this run. This would explain why the failure is isolated to this check and no sibling checks share the same message.

TERTIARY — A misconfigured or rotated AURA_STATUS_IMAGE_MODEL environment variable caused the runner to use a model (gpt-image-2 by default per line 1986) that is billed at a higher rate, accelerating limit exhaustion. This is speculative; the error message does not reference the model.

investigations.title: model-matrix eval failure: aura-gpt-5-5 returned HTTP 502 due to upstream Anthropic 429 rate-limit on POST /api/agents/.../runtime/test
investigations.summary: The model-matrix eval check failed because exactly one of two configured models, aura-gpt-5-5, received a 502 Bad Gateway from the AURA runtime harness wrapping an Anthropic 429 Too Many Requests error. The other model, aura-claude-sonnet-4-6, passed cleanly, proving the eval infrastructure itself is functional and the failure is isolated to the aura-gpt-5-5 runtime/test endpoint call at the time of the run.
investigations.rootCause: The AURA runtime harness returned HTTP 502 for the POST /api/agents/[REDACTED]/runtime/test request targeting model aura-gpt-5-5. The 502 body explicitly identifies the internal cause as a rate_limit error: the upstream Anthropic API responded with 429 Too Many Requests and the message "AURA is temporarily unable to reach the model provider. This is an issue on our side, not with your account or credits. Please try again shortly." This caused the eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1936 model loop) to record ok=false for aura-gpt-5-5, setting allPassed=false and failedModelCount=1, which violated the expected-output contract assertions at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json lines 333–334. This is an eval-layer failure reflecting a transient upstream rate-limit condition at the time of the run; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Available Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the agent pod because 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the eval runner never received a VM ID or a ready state, so all required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) is absent and the expected-output contract is entirely unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the two nodes that match the pod's affinity/selector. With 0 of 6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote-agent pod creation attempt times out unscheduled. This is an infrastructure-layer resource exhaustion on the production Kubernetes cluster, not a code defect in the eval runner or a regression in the eval configuration files. The eval failure is a direct consequence of the scheduling failure; no evidence of a user-traffic or production incident signal is present in the packet, so impact is scoped to the observability eval at this time.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots are fully consumed on the two affinity-eligible nodes: the scheduler message 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' on both eligible nodes is unambiguous. No preemption victims were found, meaning all existing VM pods are non-preemptible or at equal/higher priority.

Secondary — the node affinity or node selector on the remote-agent pod restricts scheduling to only 2 of 6 nodes, leaving no fallback capacity even if other nodes have free resources. The 4 non-matching nodes cannot be used regardless of their available capacity.

Tertiary — a prior remote-agent pod (or multiple pods) may have been created and not cleaned up, holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and preventing new allocations. The eval runner uses withCleanup, but a previous failed or leaked run could have left pods running.
Lower confidence — the cluster may have scaled down or lost one of the affinity-eligible nodes between runs, reducing total kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity below the minimum needed for a new probe pod.

investigations.title: published-observability-snapshot Eval Failure: Stale GitHub Actions Snapshot (snapshotAgeMinutes 378 > max 300)
investigations.summary: The AURA observability eval for published-observability-snapshot failed because the snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json was 378 minutes old at eval time, exceeding the contract's maximum allowed age of 300 minutes. This is a localized eval failure against the published snapshot JSON endpoint; all three sibling public-website checks (public-observability-page, public-models-page, public-marketing-pages) passed, confirming the public website itself is reachable and this failure is isolated to snapshot freshness.
investigations.rootCause: The GitHub Actions workflow responsible for regenerating and publishing the observability snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json did not run within the 300-minute window required by the expected-output contract (infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 482: snapshotAgeMinutes max 300). The snapshot was 378 minutes old when the eval ran at 2026-07-23T07:25:40Z, meaning the last successful publish occurred approximately 6 hours and 18 minutes prior. The workflow schedule, a transient runner failure, a skipped or cancelled run, or a publishing step failure are the most likely upstream causes, but the exact trigger cannot be determined from the supplied evidence alone.
proof: failed-check.message: 'snapshotAgeMinutes expected <= 300 but got 378' — the single violated assertion is snapshotAgeMinutes, all other 11 required evidence fields were present and passing (failed-check.evidence).

failed-check.evidence: snapshotAgeMinutes=378, maxAgeMinutes=300, source='github-actions', hasLiveSource=true, generatedAtPresent=true — the snapshot exists and was produced by github-actions but is stale.
expected-output.contract (infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 482): assertion { path: 'snapshotAgeMinutes', max: 300 } is the violated contract boundary.

sibling.public-observability-page, sibling.public-models-page, sibling.public-marketing-pages: all three sibling checks passed, ruling out a broad public-website infrastructure failure and localizing the issue to the snapshot publishing pipeline.

source.infra/evals/status/features.json:383: registry config shows statusImpact='informational' and required=false, confirming this eval failure does not constitute a product outage signal on its own.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=63 — the eval itself completed successfully and quickly; the failure is in the observed data value, not in eval infrastructure.
possibleCauses: The GitHub Actions workflow that publishes the observability snapshot was not triggered or did not complete successfully within the last 300 minutes, leaving the previously published snapshot in place (supported by source='github-actions' and snapshotAgeMinutes=378 in failed-check.evidence).

The GitHub Actions workflow ran but the publish step (e.g., the GitHub Pages deploy step) failed silently, so the snapshot file at the snapshotUrl was not updated even though a workflow run may appear in the Actions UI.

The workflow schedule was skipped, delayed, or cancelled — for example due to a GitHub Actions queue backlog, a branch protection event, or a manual cancellation — causing the snapshot to age past the 300-minute threshold.

A configuration mismatch exists between the registry's staleAfterMinutes=360 (infra/evals/status/features.json line 383) and the contract's snapshotAgeMinutes max=300 (infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 482): the registry considers the check stale after 360 minutes but the eval contract fails it at 300 minutes, meaning a snapshot between 300 and 360 minutes old will fail the eval but not be considered stale by the registry. This discrepancy may cause confusion about the expected refresh cadence but does not by itself explain the 378-minute age.
